idiom_name: SQLAlchemy mapped inheritance (joined / single / concrete) with polymorphic_identity
implementation_notes: SQLAlchemy builds the mapper hierarchy from the mapped classes: it supports single, joined and concrete table inheritance, with polymorphic_identity/polymorphic_on on the base mapper expressing the discriminator and polymorphic loading letting one query return objects of several types. The per-class mapper objects of the classic pattern still exist, but they are configured declaratively, and the strategy you declare is exactly the mapper shape you get (joined inheritance joins the tables on the inheritance path).
pitfalls: Only one discriminator column or expression is allowed per hierarchy: 'cascading' polymorphic identities are not supported.
Concrete table inheritance needs explicit configuration (polymorphic_union) before the hierarchy can be queried polymorphically at all.
In single table inheritance, sibling subclasses that declare the same attribute name map to the same column; conflicting declarations must be resolved with use_existing_column.

variants.name: Django multi-table inheritance (implicit OneToOneField)
variants.implementation_notes: Django's multi-table inheritance is the class-table mapper shape: each model in the hierarchy gets its own table and Django links child to parent with an implicit OneToOneField, so loading a child joins the parent table and a query against the parent returns child instances with only the parent columns populated. Abstract base classes give column reuse without a second table (concrete-style duplication), which is the cheaper choice for shallow hierarchies.
variants.code_sketch:
class Payment(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)

class CreditCardPayment(Payment):        # own table + implicit OneToOneField
    card_number = models.CharField(max_length=32)

# Payment.objects.all() returns CreditCardPayment instances (parent columns only)
# CreditCardPayment.objects.all() joins payment + creditcardpayment
pitfalls: The implicit parent link means every child save touches two tables; bulk creates become joins of inserts unless the parent row is written first.
Parent-table queries return child instances whose child fields are not loaded, so access to them costs one query per object.
Abstract base classes look like inheritance but create no parent table and no polymorphism - choosing them 'for the mapper' silently drops base-class queries.
